Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Cassino - Quick Rules 1.1 Overview 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Scoring 1.4 Card Values Cassino - Quick Rules Overview Players: 2 to 4 (4 players usually play in partnerships). Deck: Standard 52-card deck (no Jokers). Objective: Capture cards from the table to score points. The game usually ends when a player/team reaches 21 points. Gameplay Each player is dealt 4 cards face down, and 4 cards are placed face up on the table. Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn, you must play exactly one card from your hand to perform one of the following: Pairing: Play a card that matches the rank of one or more cards on the table. You capture the played card and the matching table cards. Combining: Play a card that equals the sum of two or more cards on the table (e.g., play a 9 to capture a 5 and a 4). Building: Place a card from your hand onto a table card to create a combination for your next turn. You must hold the card required to capture the build (e.g., place a 3 on a 4 and announce "Building 7" if you have a 7 in hand). An opponent can "steal" a build by increasing its value (only for "single" builds). Trailing: If you cannot or do not want to capture or build, simply place one card face up on the table. Scoring Once all cards have been played, players score points based on their captured pile: Most Cards: 3 points (0 if tied). Most Spades: 1 point (0 if tied). 10 of Diamonds (Big Cassino): 2 points. 2 of Spades (Little Cassino): 1 point. Each Ace: 1 point (4 points total). Card Values Number Cards (2–10): Represent their face value. Aces: Count as 1. Face Cards (J, Q, K): Have no numerical value. They can only be captured by pairing (e.g., a King captures a King), not by combinations. [Rating: 3/10] A welcome change from the usual trick-taking and melding card games, but, once you've played a couple games, it seems to come down mostly to luck.

[Rating: 3/10] The people I know who like this described being delighted to find an older game that felt modern to them. I didn't experience that at all-- but I've also now played a few modernized variants on Casino and didn't enjoy them either. So it's probably just not the gametype for me. Even given that, though, I don't remember anything seeming special in the classic version.  [1 play]

[Rating: 3/10] Like Koi-Koi, this will often see one player accomplish little but feeding their opponent. Unlike Koi-Koi, this has no novelty value for the Westerner.

[Rating: 3/10] Casino is a traditional card game about fishing, in which players use their cards in hands to gain cards from the table, directly, by matching the types or sum, or also by forming builds of cards, which players may take by playing a card which matches the total sum of the cards in the build.  Scoring is as such: whoever has the most cards gets three points; whoever has most Spades is one point; each Ace is worth one point; the ten of diamonds, called Big Casino or the Good Ten, is worth two points; the two of spades, called Little Casino or the Good Two, is worth one point. [Rating: 4/10] Fair.  I went through a phase where I loved to play this.  It's a nice little card game that has more opportunities for skill than appear at first glance.

[Rating: 4/10] Not a terrible standard card game. I've played it a lot and there are some tactics available, but the skills that make the most difference by far are card-counting and probability calculations. Far too much luck, however. Whoever gets dealt the 10 diamonds will win that card at least 80% of the time. In fact, avoiding playing cards that make 10s and or potential further builds to 10s is a tactic that should have a greater chance of success than it does. Overall, OK.

[Rating: 4/10] Played one 3-player game while waiting for a Tichu fourth. Like Cribbage in the sense that a better player can play a bit better, but you're really at the mercy of the cards. One play lef me with no urge for a second play.

[Rating: 4/10] This is my best friend's families' official 2-player game.  I learned it while visiting there.  It's a pretty good game, especially if you're two and only have a deck of cards.  My rating reflects my interest in playing, which is low, but not completely uninterested.

[Rating: 4/10] My mother loves this game to death, but it doesn't have enough strategy to me whether two-player or on teams. It always seems like I win exactly 50% of the time.

[Rating: 4/10] I liked this well enough as a kid, but suspect it would now feel mechanical and random.

It IS a good game.  100419 Its fun, but to be honest I think I'd rather play something else in a 2P situation...and if there are more players then I'd pull out other board games.

[Rating: 4/10] There is not a tremendous amount of strategy in this game, except for making sure to count cards.  The rules are fairly simple, which helps the rating, but then you have to remember some weird cards for scoring (like the 2 of spades and the 10 of diamonds), which hurts the rating.  Overall, I don't think it is that interesting of a game.
